name: Butter Chicken
genericFact: Butter chicken (murgh makhani) is widely credited to Delhi restaurant kitchens in the 1950s, built to use up leftover tandoori chicken.

swaps.tip: Use 2 tbsp cream (or blended soaked cashews) instead of 1/2 cup, and half the butter. Grill or tandoor the chicken first instead of pan-frying it in oil.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala
genericFact: The exact origin of chicken tikka masala is disputed between India and the UK.

swaps.tip: Cut the added salt in half and build flavor with more garam masala, kasuri methi and a squeeze of lemon. Use no-salt-added tomato purée.

name: Palak Paneer
genericFact: Paneer is a fresh cheese that doesn't melt, which is why it holds its shape in curries.

swaps.tip: Use half paneer and half tofu or chickpeas, replace the cream with a splash of milk or blended cashews, and temper the spices in just 1 tsp of ghee.

name: Chana Masala
genericFact: Chickpeas make chana masala one of the best fiber and plant-protein dishes in Indian cooking.

name: Dal Tadka
genericFact: The 'tadka' is spices bloomed in hot oil or ghee and poured over the dal at the end.

name: Chicken Biryani
genericFact: Biryani is layered and slow-steamed (dum), so the rice absorbs the spices from the meat.

swaps.tip: Aim for equal parts rice and chicken-vegetable masala, or swap in parboiled brown basmati. Serve with raita and a kachumber salad.
Salt the rice water lightly and let whole spices (cardamom, cloves, bay leaf) and baked fried onions do the flavoring.

name: Naan
genericFact: Traditional naan is baked on the wall of a tandoor oven at very high heat.

name: Samosas
genericFact: Samosas likely traveled to India from Central Asia centuries ago.

swaps.tip: Bake or air-fry the samosas, brushing the pastry with a little oil, and fill with more peas and potato than fried onion.

name: Masala Dosa
genericFact: Dosa batter is fermented rice and lentils, which gives the crepe its tang.

swaps.tip: Cook on a well-seasoned non-stick tawa with a teaspoon of oil or ghee instead of ladling it over, and keep the potato filling light on oil.

name: Idli
genericFact: Idli is steamed rather than fried, which keeps it very low in fat.

name: Gulab Jamun
genericFact: Gulab jamun is soaked in sugar syrup, which is where most of its sugar comes from.

swaps.tip: Use a thinner syrup (1 part sugar to 2 parts water) scented with cardamom and rose water, soak the jamuns briefly, and enjoy one or two.

name: Mango Lassi
genericFact: Lassi is a yogurt drink, so mango lassi adds some protein and calcium to the sugar.

swaps.tip: Use fully ripe mango for sweetness and skip the added sugar. Blend with plain low-fat yogurt and a pinch of cardamom.

name: Chole Bhature
genericFact: Bhature is deep-fried leavened bread, which is why this plate is so calorie-dense.

swaps.tip: Swap the deep-fried bhature for a griddled whole-wheat kulcha or roti.
Serve the chole with one bhatura (or a roti) and a big cucumber-onion salad.
Use dry-roasted spices like anardana and amchur for tang so you need less salt, and cook the chickpeas from scratch.

name: Chicken Burrito
genericFact: A restaurant burrito can hold several servings of rice, beans and cheese in a single tortilla.

swaps.tip: Go light on sour cream and cheese, and add pico de gallo, grilled peppers and a few slices of avocado for richness.
Make it a burrito bowl, or use one smaller whole-wheat tortilla filled with more beans and vegetables than rice.
Cook rice and beans with cumin, garlic, lime and cilantro, rinse canned beans, and skip pre-seasoned meats.

name: Beef Tacos
genericFact: Street-style tacos use small corn tortillas, so the filling is the main source of fat.

swaps.tip: Use lean ground beef or shredded chicken, drain the fat, warm the corn tortillas on a dry comal instead of frying them, and top with onion, cilantro and lime.

name: Chicken Enchiladas
genericFact: Enchiladas are tortillas rolled around filling and covered in chile sauce, often with melted cheese.

swaps.tip: Use half the cheese and a lean shredded-chicken filling, and dip the tortillas in sauce rather than frying them.
Make the sauce from dried ancho and guajillo chiles instead of using canned enchilada sauce.

name: Guacamole
genericFact: Most of guacamole's fat is the unsaturated fat found in avocado.

name: Chilaquiles
genericFact: Chilaquiles are traditionally made from leftover tortillas, fried and simmered in salsa.

swaps.tip: Bake the tortilla triangles until crisp instead of frying them, and top with an egg, beans and a little queso fresco.
Use a homemade salsa roja and go easy on the cheese and crema.

name: Refried Beans
genericFact: 'Refried' comes from 'refritos', which means well-fried rather than fried twice.

name: Pork Tamale
genericFact: Tamales are steamed in corn husks, a technique with roots going back thousands of years in Mesoamerica.

name: Pozole Rojo
genericFact: Pozole is built on hominy, corn treated with lime (nixtamalization), which makes its niacin available.

swaps.tip: Use low-sodium broth, rinse canned hominy, and season with toasted dried chiles, oregano and lime at the table.

name: Elote (Street Corn)
genericFact: Elote takes humble grilled corn and adds mayo, cotija cheese, lime and chile.

name: Churros
genericFact: Churros are fried dough, so most of their fat comes from the frying oil.

name: Cheese Quesadilla
genericFact: Cheese is the main source of fat and sodium in a quesadilla.

swaps.tip: Use less cheese (a little Oaxaca melts well), fill half the tortilla with peppers, mushrooms or beans, and cook on a dry comal.
Choose a lower-sodium cheese like queso fresco and add salsa for flavor instead of salt.

name: Horchata
genericFact: Horchata is traditionally made from rice and cinnamon, with sugar added to taste.

swaps.tip: Cut the sugar by half and lean on cinnamon and vanilla for flavor, using unsweetened rice milk as the base.

name: Spaghetti Carbonara
genericFact: Authentic carbonara uses egg, cured pork and pecorino, with no cream.

swaps.tip: Use less guanciale or pancetta (render it and discard some fat) and make the sauce with whole eggs plus starchy pasta water. Pecorino gives big flavor in small amounts.
Use a smaller portion of pasta (about 3/4 cup cooked) and add peas, asparagus or zucchini. Whole-wheat spaghetti adds fiber.
Pecorino and cured pork are already salty, so salt the pasta water lightly and skip any extra salt.

name: Lasagna
genericFact: Lasagna layers pasta, ragù, béchamel and cheese, so one slice packs carbs, protein and fat.

swaps.tip: Use part-skim ricotta and mozzarella, lean beef or turkey in the ragù, and add spinach or zucchini layers.
Use no-salt-added tomatoes and let basil, oregano and parmesan do the seasoning.

name: Margherita Pizza
genericFact: Margherita pizza is said to be named after Queen Margherita of Savoy, who visited Naples in 1889.

swaps.tip: Go for a thin Neapolitan-style crust and pair a slice or two with a big arugula salad.
Stick with fresh mozzarella and fresh basil, and go light on salty cured toppings.

name: Penne Arrabbiata
genericFact: 'Arrabbiata' means angry, a nod to the chili heat in the sauce.

swaps.tip: Serve a smaller pasta portion topped with extra sauce, or use whole-wheat or chickpea penne.

name: Mushroom Risotto
genericFact: Stirring risotto releases starch from the arborio rice, which creates its creaminess without cream.

swaps.tip: Use less arborio and bulk up with mushrooms and spring vegetables, or make an orzotto with pearl barley.
Use low-sodium or homemade stock and finish with just a little parmesan.

name: Minestrone
genericFact: Minestrone is a vegetable and bean soup, which is why it's high in fiber.

swaps.tip: Use homemade or low-sodium stock and simmer a parmesan rind in the pot for savory depth.

name: Caprese Salad
genericFact: Caprese salad wears the colors of the Italian flag: red tomato, white mozzarella, green basil.

swaps.tip: Use part-skim fresh mozzarella, add more tomato, and drizzle olive oil sparingly with a little balsamic.

name: Bruschetta
genericFact: 'Bruschetta' comes from the Roman dialect word for roasting over coals.

name: Chicken Parmigiana
genericFact: Chicken parmigiana is an Italian-American take on the southern Italian eggplant parmigiana.

swaps.tip: Bake the breaded cutlet on a rack instead of frying it, and use less mozzarella on top.
Use a homemade marinara and a lighter hand with the cheese.

name: Tiramisu
genericFact: Tiramisu means 'pick me up' in Italian, a nod to the espresso.

swaps.tip: Lighten the mascarpone with Greek yogurt or whipped egg whites, and dip the savoiardi quickly in espresso.
Use less sugar in the cream and finish with cocoa, which is naturally unsweetened.

name: Gelato
genericFact: Gelato typically has less fat than American ice cream because it uses more milk than cream.

name: Gnocchi with Tomato Sauce
genericFact: Gnocchi are small dumplings, usually made from potato and flour.

swaps.tip: Make gnudi with spinach and ricotta (less flour), or serve a smaller portion of gnocchi with plenty of vegetables.

name: Kung Pao Chicken
genericFact: Kung pao chicken gets its numbing kick from Sichuan peppercorns.

swaps.tip: Stir-fry with 1 tbsp of oil, use fewer peanuts (toast them for flavor), and add celery and bell pepper.
Use low-sodium soy sauce and let dried chiles, Sichuan peppercorn and black vinegar carry the flavor.

name: Pork Fried Rice
genericFact: Fried rice began as a way to use up leftover rice.

swaps.tip: Use half the rice and double the vegetables and egg. Day-old brown rice works well.
Use low-sodium soy sauce and season with white pepper, scallion and a little sesame oil.

name: General Tso's Chicken
genericFact: General Tso's chicken is mostly an American-Chinese creation.

swaps.tip: Air-fry or bake the chicken instead of deep-frying it.
Serve with a smaller portion of rice and extra steamed broccoli.
Make the sauce with low-sodium soy sauce, and use less of it.
Cut the sugar in the sauce by half and add rice vinegar and ginger for balance.

name: Steamed Pork Dumplings
genericFact: Steamed dumplings skip the frying oil that potstickers get.

name: Beef and Broccoli
genericFact: The broccoli adds vitamin C, a nutrient the beef doesn't provide.

swaps.tip: Use low-sodium soy sauce and thin the sauce with stock and cornstarch instead of extra soy or oyster sauce.

name: Mapo Tofu
genericFact: Mapo tofu's numbing heat comes from Sichuan peppercorn and chili bean paste.

swaps.tip: Use less chili oil and half the ground pork, or replace some of it with mushrooms.
Use less doubanjiang (the salty bean paste) and low-sodium stock. Sichuan peppercorn adds flavor without salt.

name: Hot and Sour Soup
genericFact: Hot and sour soup gets most of its sodium from soy sauce and stock.

swaps.tip: Use low-sodium stock, and get the sour from rice vinegar and the heat from white pepper rather than more soy sauce.

name: Egg Rolls
genericFact: Egg rolls are deep-fried, which adds most of their fat.

swaps.tip: Bake or air-fry the rolls with the wrappers brushed in a little oil, and fill with more cabbage and carrot.

name: Chicken Chow Mein
genericFact: 'Chow mein' means stir-fried noodles.

swaps.tip: Use 1 tbsp of oil and more vegetables, and don't pre-fry the noodles.
Use half the noodles and double the cabbage, bean sprouts and carrots.
Use low-sodium soy sauce and add garlic and ginger for flavor.

name: Congee
genericFact: Congee is a rice porridge eaten across Asia, often for breakfast or when feeling unwell.

name: Sweet and Sour Pork
genericFact: Sweet and sour sauce is largely sugar, vinegar and ketchup.

swaps.tip: Bake or air-fry the pork instead of deep-frying it.
Serve with a smaller portion of rice and extra stir-fried vegetables.
Use low-sodium soy sauce and less sauce overall.
Sweeten the sauce with pineapple juice and use less sugar and ketchup.

name: Peking Duck with Pancakes
genericFact: Peking duck is prized for its crisp skin, which is also where much of the fat lives.

swaps.tip: Enjoy the skin in moderation and add extra cucumber and scallion to each pancake.
Use less hoisin sauce (it's sweet and salty) and let the fresh cucumber and scallion add flavor.

name: Garlic Bok Choy
genericFact: Bok choy is a cruciferous vegetable and a good source of vitamin C.

name: Tonkotsu Ramen
genericFact: Tonkotsu broth is made by boiling pork bones for hours, which makes it rich in fat and sodium.

swaps.tip: Choose a shoyu or shio ramen broth, which is lighter than creamy tonkotsu, and skip the extra back-fat.
Eat about half the noodles and add extra vegetables, egg and bean sprouts.
Drink only some of the broth. Most of the sodium is in the soup.

name: Chicken Teriyaki with Rice
genericFact: 'Teriyaki' means glossy grilled; the glaze is soy sauce, mirin and sugar.

swaps.tip: Serve with a smaller rice portion (or half brown rice) and extra steamed vegetables.
Make the teriyaki sauce at home with low-sodium soy sauce, mirin and ginger.
Use less mirin and sugar in the glaze and let grated ginger and a squeeze of citrus add brightness.

name: Salmon Nigiri
genericFact: Nigiri is one of the lighter sushi choices: fish on a small bed of seasoned rice.

name: Shrimp & Veggie Tempura
genericFact: Tempura batter is kept cold and lightly mixed so it fries up crisp.

swaps.tip: Use ice-cold sparkling water for a thin, light batter, or air-fry with a light panko coating.

name: Miso Soup
genericFact: Miso is fermented soybean paste and the main source of this soup's sodium.

swaps.tip: Use a little less miso paste (or a reduced-sodium miso) and add tofu, wakame and scallions for volume.

name: Tonkatsu
genericFact: Tonkatsu is a panko-breaded, deep-fried pork cutlet, usually served with shredded cabbage.

swaps.tip: Bake or air-fry the panko-coated cutlet on a rack, and trim the fat from the pork loin.

name: Onigiri
genericFact: Onigiri are rice balls, a classic portable meal in Japan.

name: Gyudon (Beef Bowl)
genericFact: Gyudon is a rice bowl topped with beef and onion simmered in sweet soy broth.

swaps.tip: Use thinly sliced lean beef and skim the fat off the simmering broth.
Serve a smaller bowl of rice with more onion, and add a side of vegetables.
Use low-sodium soy sauce and dashi, and go easy on the sauce poured over the rice.

name: Edamame
genericFact: Edamame is immature soybeans, a complete plant protein.

name: Takoyaki
genericFact: Takoyaki are octopus-filled batter balls that come from Osaka.

swaps.tip: Use less sauce and mayonnaise, and add more cabbage and scallion inside the batter.

name: Okonomiyaki
genericFact: 'Okonomiyaki' means 'grilled as you like it'.

swaps.tip: Use less oil on the griddle, choose lean pork or shrimp instead of pork belly, and go light on the mayo.
Use less okonomiyaki sauce and add bonito flakes and aonori for flavor instead.

name: Mochi
genericFact: Mochi is made from pounded glutinous rice.

name: Katsu Curry
genericFact: Japanese curry roux is made with flour and fat, which adds a lot of calories.

swaps.tip: Bake the katsu, and use a lighter curry roux (or make one with less oil) loaded with extra vegetables.
Serve a smaller rice portion and bulk up the curry with carrot, onion and other vegetables.
Use half the roux block and thin the curry with low-sodium stock.

name: Falafel
genericFact: Falafel is made from ground chickpeas or fava beans and deep-fried.

swaps.tip: Bake or air-fry the falafel and add extra fresh parsley and cilantro to the mix for flavor.

name: Hummus
genericFact: Hummus pairs chickpea protein and fiber with tahini's fat.

name: Chicken Shawarma Wrap
genericFact: Shawarma is meat roasted on a vertical spit and shaved off in thin slices.

swaps.tip: Use trimmed chicken thigh or breast, grill it, and swap garlic sauce for a lighter yogurt-tahini sauce.
Make the spice rub (cumin, coriander, cardamom, paprika) yourself with less salt, and go light on pickles and sauce.

name: Tabbouleh
genericFact: Authentic tabbouleh is mostly parsley, with just a little bulgur.

name: Baba Ghanoush
genericFact: Baba ghanoush is smoky roasted eggplant blended with tahini.

name: Lamb Kofta
genericFact: Kofta is seasoned ground meat shaped onto skewers and grilled.

swaps.tip: Use lean lamb (or half lamb, half turkey) mixed with grated onion and parsley, and grill on a rack so the fat drips away.

name: Shakshuka
genericFact: Shakshuka is eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce.

swaps.tip: Use 1 tbsp of olive oil and fewer feta crumbles.
Use no-salt-added crushed tomatoes and season with cumin, paprika and fresh herbs.

name: Mujaddara
genericFact: Mujaddara pairs lentils with rice and tops them with caramelized onions.

swaps.tip: Use more lentils than rice, swap in brown rice or bulgur, and serve with a fresh salad.

name: Baklava
genericFact: Baklava layers phyllo with nuts and is soaked in syrup.

swaps.tip: Use fewer phyllo layers and brush them with olive oil instead of lots of butter.
Use a lighter syrup flavored with lemon and orange blossom, and serve smaller pieces.

name: Pita Bread
genericFact: Pita's pocket forms when steam puffs the dough during baking.

name: Fattoush
genericFact: Fattoush is a bread salad that turns stale pita into crisp croutons.

name: Lentil Soup (Shorbat Adas)
genericFact: Lentils are among the highest-fiber legumes.

swaps.tip: Use homemade or low-sodium stock and brighten the soup with lemon and cumin.
